intro: Lesson 96: Electrical units, Q = It and two resistors in series. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Two resistors are in series with a 9 V supply. The current in the first is 0.3 A. What is the current in the second?
questions.a: B) 0.3 A. In a series circuit the same current flows through every component.

questions.q: Two resistors of 5 Ω and 10 Ω in series. Total?
Big question: why does a second resistor in series make the current smaller?
questions.a: Total resistance increases, so for the same voltage the current is lower (I = V ÷ R).

questions.q: A 4 Ω and 8 Ω resistor in series with 6 V. Find current.
questions.model: Total resistance first: 4 + 8 = 12 Ω. Then I = V ÷ R = 6 ÷ 12 = 0.5 A.

questions.q: Five series circuit problems (portal worksheet): total R, current, each voltage.
questions.a: Answers in the key, e.g. 10 Ω + 20 Ω on 9 V: 30 Ω, 0.3 A, 3 V and 6 V.
questions.model: Teacher does problem 1: 10 + 20 = 30 Ω; I = 9 ÷ 30 = 0.3 A; V₁ = 3 V; V₂ = 6 V; check 3 + 6 = 9 V.

questions.q: A charge of 90 C flows through a series circuit in 3 minutes. Current?
In series, a 6 Ω resistor has 3 V across it on a 12 V supply. Find the other resistor.
questions.a: I = 0.5 A; other voltage 9 V; R = 9 ÷ 0.5 = 18 Ω
